summary: Regression run after the code-quality refactor, backend only. Full suite in /app/backend/tests: 36/37 pass. The one failure is TestAI::test_recommend_bn. It asserts source=='ai' but got 'rules' with ai_reason 'failed'. Cause: Gemini fails on every model (ClientError 429 quota, plus one TimeoutError in backend.err.log), the same environment problem as in iteration 2. The refactor did not cause it. New test_iteration3_refactor.py: 13/13 pass. It checks: all 21 seed ids load; ab-pmjay application_url is beneficiary.nha.gov.in and pmmy's is jansamarth.in, with the correct official_url; mode, states and exclusions are passed through **opts correctly; the farmer-WB match returns pm-kisan, krishak-bandhu and pmfby, with pm-kisan 'strong'; a taxpayer is excluded from pm-kisan with failed=['taxpayer'...]; unknown answers become pending; recommend best_scheme_id is always in the top-5 candidates; scheme_ids narrowing works; no candidates gives source 'none'. The 5 split admin CRUD tests (create/read, update, verify, archive hides, restore), auth roles, saved isolation and explain?lang=hi all pass. Code review of the diff: behaviour is the same. _known_values now guards None, which is equivalent. _ai_recommendation now also handles rec None safely.

critical.issue: Gemini quota/availability is still failing (429 ClientError on gemini-3.8/3.7/3.5-flash). Every recommendation falls back to rules. Not a refactor regression.

minor.issue: The test hard-asserts source=='ai', so it fails whenever Gemini is down. Consider asserting source in ('ai','rules'), or skipping when ai_reason=='failed'.

action_items: Restore the Gemini quota/billing, or use a key with quota.
Optionally make TestAI::test_recommend_bn tolerant of the rules fallback.
critical_code_review_comments: _ai_response uses next() with no default. It is safe only because _ai_recommendation checks best_scheme_id against the candidates, which are built from ranked. Keep that coupling, or add a default to avoid StopIteration.
In matching.match, the result tuple uses `(excluded if bad else results).append(bad or result)`, which is correct but terse. A plain if/else would read more clearly.

success_rate.backend: 98% (49/50; the only failure is caused by the Gemini quota, not the refactor)

seed_data_creation: None. The admin CRUD tests create TEST_ schemes and delete them in their own teardown.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Run: cd /app/backend/tests && python -m pytest . -c /app/backend/pytest.ini -v -o addopts=''. test_recommend_bn depends on Gemini quota. Last checked: Gemini still returns 429.
